Reference Petition U/s 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

JUDGMENT BRIEF FACTS:-
1.) This judgment shall decide the reference petition no.
44/2016 preferred by petitioners, Sh. Nand Lal and Sh. Om Prakash for the enhancement of the compensation against compulsory acquisition of his shop bearing No.1/1144 measuring 16.72 square meters, situated in Chandrawali @ Shahdara, Delhi vide Award No. 01/1999-2000 dated 20.07.1999, passed by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as 'LAC'), Shahdara,
Delhi.
2.)

To decide the reference U/s 18 L.A. Act r/w statement U/s 19 of the Act sent by the LAC Delhi,
the relevant dates and facts which are necessary for adjudication in the present matter are being given herein under:-
i) Date of notification U/s 4 of the Act : 12.06.1997 ii) Date of notification U/s 6 of the Act : 28.07.1997 iii) Date of award : 20.07.1999 iv) Area of the locality : Chandrawali @ Shahdara v) Project : MRTS, Delhi vi) The land use of area as per award : Residential vii) Petition referred to court on : 10.08.2010 LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs.
Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 2 of 14 BACKGROUND:-

3 . ) The petitioners being owner of shop bearing No.1/1144 measuring 16.72 square meters consisting of basement shop and ground floor in khasra no.446 min, situated in the revenue estate of Village Chandrawali @ Shahdara, Delhi, filed the present reference against the award No.1/1999-2000 passed on 20.07.1999, thereby assessing the market value of the land @ Rs.2805/-
per sq.mt. which is not acceptable to the petitioners.

sentences.text: The petitioners were doing business on the said property under the name and style of "Matta Cycle Works" for commercial purposes in which they were dealing in sale and purchase of new cycles and their parts.
Both the shops have class 'A' construction and were fully renovated with wood work, marble work etc.

Further, other than LRs of deceased petitioner no.1 and petitioner no.2, no other person has any right, title or interest in the shops and only LRs of deceased petitioner are entitled to compensation/enhanced compensation.
The petitioners are not satisfied with the compensation amount awarded by the LAC, determination of market value of land in question, measurement of land etc.

ii. The LAC has mistakenly assessed the market value of land and structures of petitioners at low rates which does not represents the market value of the land on the date of notification U/s 4 of LA, Act.

The market value was assessed by the LAC without any inquiry and without LAC No.44/16 Sh.
Nand Lal & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 3 of 14 considering the demand and supply.

entities.text: Nand Lal & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 3 of 14
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
iii. The LAC has wrongly assessed the market value of land in question @ Rs.2805/-
per sq.mt. whereas as on the date of notification U/s 4, L.A. Act, the market value of the shops was much more than Rs.60,00,000/-.
The market value of the land alone was more than Rs.2,00,000/-.

iv. The LAC has failed to consider that the property in question us a built up commercial property located on Main Bazaar Road, Railway Road, Shahdara, which is prestigious and famous market and no land is available for sale in this area and in its vicinity at any price.

All facilities and amenities like electricity, water, mettled road, banks, Railway Station etc. were available prior to the date of notification U/s 4, L.A. Act.
v.
The LAC has further failed to consider the sale rates of commercial properties in the vicinity.
Even the sale consideration of properties sold by DDA and other agencies has not been considered.
vi. In addition, LAC has failed to appreciate that land in question were situated in the main market, Railway Road, Shahdara and surrounded by fully developed market from all sides.

All the amenities like electricity, mettled road, water, sewage, railway station, banks highway etc. were available prior to the date of notification U/s 4, L.A.
Act.
Even Shahdara Railway Station is about 15-20 sq.yds. away from the acquired land.
Banks, NH no.1, cinema halls, hospitals, Old Shahdara Court etc. were also situated near the acquired land.

Further, two hospitals, namely, Chandiwala Hospital and Civil Hospital situated at a LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 4 of 14 distance of 20-25 sq.yds. from market under reference.
vii. The LAC has not considered that properties in question were assessed to tax on commercial rates and had commercial electricity/ water connections.
The LAC has not appreciated that Main Bazaar Market, Railway Road, Shahdara is one of the oldest market of Trans Yamuna Area.

sentences.text: The market value of the acquired land at the time of notification U/s 4 was Rs.2 lakhs per sq. meter.

The petitioners claimed the same for their acquired properties and in addition, petitioners claimed Rs.25,00,000/- for loss on business and goodwill; Rs.1,00,000/- for shifting charges and Rs.1,00,000/- for fittings and fixtures.
In view of the above reasons, this reference was filed by the petitioners before this Court.

4.) Notices of the reference petition were issued to the respondents and on completion of service, the respondents had put their appearance/(s), before the Court, through Counsel and had filed their separate written statements, in the matter.
5.) In the written statement, Land Acquisition Collector(Shahdara)/respondent No.1 that notification U/s 4 of the Act was issued on 12.06.1997 for acquisition of 41 bigha land.
The declaration U/s 6 & 17 of the Act were issued on 28.07.1997.
The land has been acquired for the public purpose namely Mass Rapid Transit System Project.

Notices U/s 9 & 10 were issued to the land owners/interested persons, inviting claims of the affected properties and in pursuance thereof, number of claims were filed by the affected persons, claiming different LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 5 of 14 value of the land and properties.
Necessary demarcation was carried out at the spot and it was revealed that total area was 39 bigha and 10 biswas instead of 41 bigha, as shown in notification U/ 4 & 6 of Act.
There was difference of 1 bigha and 10 biswa, as the actual area of khasra No. was 12 bigha and 6 biswa.

After considering all the claims, LAC had made and announced the award U/s 11 of LA Act bearing No.1/1999-2000 on 20.07.1999.
6.)
The claim of the petitioners with respect to measurements, apportionment and compensation of land is admitted to the extent of section 19 statement of LAC.
The compensation assessed by LAC is sufficient and reasonable and it reflects the true market value prevailing at the time of notification issued U/s 4 of Act.

Various factors were taken into account while assessing the market value, previous award of the same village and also gave due appreciation to assess the market value of the land for the corresponding period.
LAC has assessed fair market value of the land @ Rs.2850 per sq. meter besides other statutory benefits.
The petitioners have claimed excessive and exorbitant market value of the land and structures.

The LAC has considered the market value of the land on the date of publication of notification U/s 4 of Act i.e.
12.06.1997.
The Slum Area Improvement and Clearance Act is applicable to the land in dispute.

sentences.text: Petitioners are not entitled for enhanced compensation on the land in question.
LAC has taken into consideration all the factors including location and potentiality of the land while assessing the market value of the land.
The present reference petition is filed beyond the period of limitation and therefore, liable to be dismissed with cost.

8.) During pendency of the case, an application U/s 151 CPC was moved on behalf of the LRs of petitioner no.1 stating that petitioner no.1- Sh. Nand Lal had expired on 04.07.2001 leaving behind three LRs- Om Prakash (petitioner no.2 herein), Subhash Chand and Raj Kumar.
It is further stated that Smt. Shanti Devi, widow of petitioner no.1 and Subhash Chand, S/o petitioner no.1 had already relinquished their shares in favour of petitioner no.2- Sh. Om Prakash.
The said application was allowed vide order dated 05.08.2015 and the LRs of deceased petitioner no.1 were impleaded as petitioners in the present case.

9.) From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 27.08.2015:-
a) Whether the petitioners have any right, title or interest in the land in question?

OPP.
b) What was the market value of the land in question at the time of issuance of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act?
Onus on parties c) Whether the petition is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
OPP d) Relief.

Accordingly, my issue-wise findings are as follows:-
ISSUE NO.1:
"Whether the petitioners have any right, title or interest in the land in question?
OPP"
a) The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.

In support of this issue, petitioners have relied upon the reference judgment U/s 30-31, L.A. Act vide Ex.PW4/A wherein the share of the deceased petitioner- Sh. Nand Lal was determined to the extent of 20 sq.yds. to be divided in equal shares in favour of the petitioners- Raj Kumar and Om Prakash (both sons of Sh. Nand Lal).

The relevant para of the said judgment is reproduced herein:-
"In view of my findings on issue no.1, Sh. Om Prakash and Sh. Raj Kumar both sons of Lt. Sh. Nand Lal, IP no.444 are entitled for compensation for the land measuring 20 sq.yds. (area as mentioned in the conveyance deed) in respect of property no.1/1144, Railway Road, Shahdara, Delhi-110032 in equal shares at the rate of notified in the award along with other statutory benefits as mentioned in the award as well as structure compensation amounting to Rs.1,26,943/- (Rupees one lac twenty LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 10 of 14 six thousand nine hundred forty three only) in equal shares.
Report of amount payable to claimants be called from District Nazir".

b) Accordingly, since the right, title and interest of the petitioners in the land in question has already been decided vide Ex.PW4/A and presumed to be attained finality as remained undisputed during the trial, it is held that the petitioners, namely, Sh. Raj Kumar and Sh. Om Prakash have right, title and interest in the land in question for compensation as held by the Ld. Court vide judgment Ex.PW4/A. ISSUE NO.2:
"What was the market value of land in question at the time of issuance of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act?
Onus on parties"
AND ISSUE NO.3 "Whether the petition is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?

During the course of argument,
counsels for the parties have apprised this Court that market value with respect to the land acquired vide the same notification and same award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 07.06.2019 passed in the case titled as "Union of India Vs. M.L. Gupta & Ors.' in which the Hon'ble High Court has fixed the market value of the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtr. along-with statutory benefits.

sentences.text: Even otherwise, two equals cannot be treated unequally.

Reliance in this regard can be placed upon the judgment titled as 'Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. Vs. State of J&K' reported in AIR 2017 SC 1518 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court wherein it is held that "when the acquired lands are identical and similar and the acquisition is for the same purpose,
it would not be proper to discriminate between the land owners unless there are strong reasons".

In these circumstances, this Court is not inclined to go into any evidences or judgments relied upon by the parties to the instant petition in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court in case titled as 'Union of India Vs.
M.L. Gupta' wherein the market value for the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award have already been assessed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e. 12.06.1997.

sentences.text: Even otherwise, nothing substantial has been brought on record by either side to differ from the market value assessed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in one of the matters arising out of the same award and pertaining to the identical land.

c) Though respondent no.2- DMRC further argued that the SLP against the order of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the said case is still pending before the Hon'ble Supreme Court with respect to the determination of market value, however from the perusal of the record, it is observed that SLP filed by the respondents has already been dismissed, however, SLP filed by the petitioner, namely, Sh. M.L. Gupta is still pending adjudication.
Thus, market value assessed by the Hon'ble High Court has reached finality qua the respondents.

Therefore, in the LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal &
Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 12 of 14 totality of circumstances, it is held that market value of the land in question acquired vide the same notification and same award is fixed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtr. on the date of notification i.e. 12.06.1997 along-with statutory benefits.

sentences.text: In view of the findings on issue no.1, the petition/ reference filed U/s 18 of L.A. Act, is allowed.
The petitioners had claimed compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- per sq.mt., which is now fixed and allowed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mt.

The petitioners are entitled to the market value @ Rs.4692/- per ) Sh. Nand Lal (Since Deceased) vs Union Of India on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182853182/
8 sq.mt. as on 12.06.1997 with respect to their share determined in the total land acquired i.e. 16.72 sq. mtrs. (20 sq.yds.) as per the judgment in reference U/s 30-31, L.A. Act vide Ex.PW4/A.
b)
According to the award, solatium was allowed @ 30%.
Accordingly, the solatium is also allowed @ 30% on the market value, as determined above, as per provisions of L.A. Act, 1894.
c) The petitioners have also claimed interest, as per law.

According to the award, 12% interest was allowed on the market value, fixed by the LAC U/s 23(1)A of LA Act, 1894 from the date of notification U/s 4 of Act (12.06.1997) till the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999.
Accordingly, the same is also allowed on the present market value, fixed as above.

d) According to the award, interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894 LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs.
Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 13 of 14 was also allowed observing that DMRC had taken the land on 12.06.1997 and as such petitioners are entitled to interest on the balance amount, as per section 34 of LA Act, 1894 @ 9% per annum from the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999 till expiry of one year and thereafter, @ 15% per annum till payment or deposited into the Court.
The same is also allowed on the enhanced market value of the land in question, as determined above.
The respondent nos.1 and 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation as determined hereinabove to the petitioners.

e) The above reliefs are subject to the deductions of compensation / solatium / additional benefits /
interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894, which have already been received by the petitioners/ LRs of petitioner, as were fixed by the LAC vide Award No. 01/1999-2000 dated 20.07.1999.
f)
The reference petition stands answered accordingly.
Both the parties will bear their own costs.
A copy of this judgment be sent to LAC concerned to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation to the petitioners within three months from today.
No order as to cost.
File be consigned to the record room.

Nand Lal & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 3 of 14 considering the demand and supply.
After considering all the claims, LAC had made and announced the award U/s 11 of LA Act bearing No.1/1999-2000 on 20.07.1999.
6.)
The claim of the petitioners with respect to measurements, apportionment and compensation of land is admitted to the extent of section 19 statement of LAC.
The compensation assessed by LAC is sufficient and reasonable and it reflects the true market value prevailing at the time of notification issued U/s 4 of Act.
Various factors were taken into account while assessing the market value, previous award of the same village and also gave due appreciation to assess the market value of the land for the corresponding period.
LAC has assessed fair market value of the land @ Rs.2850 per sq. meter besides other statutory benefits.
The petitioners have claimed excessive and exorbitant market value of the land and structures.
The LAC has considered the market value of the land on the date of publication of notification U/s 4 of Act i.e.
12.06.1997.
It is averred in the written statement filed on behalf of DMRC Ltd. i.e. respondent No.2 that compensation has been LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 6 of 14 correctly assessed by the LAC.
Petitioners are not entitled for enhanced compensation on the land in question.
LAC has taken into consideration all the factors including location and potentiality of the land while assessing the market value of the land.
opennyai_summary.issue:
9.) From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 27.08.2015:-
a) Whether the petitioners have any right, title or interest in the land in question?
OPP.
b) What was the market value of the land in question at the time of issuance of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act?
Onus on parties c) Whether the petition is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
Accordingly, my issue-wise findings are as follows:-
ISSUE NO.1:
"Whether the petitioners have any right, title or interest in the land in question?
OPP"
a) The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
b) Accordingly, since the right, title and interest of the petitioners in the land in question has already been decided vide Ex.PW4/A and presumed to be attained finality as remained undisputed during the trial, it is held that the petitioners, namely, Sh. Raj Kumar and Sh. Om Prakash have right, title and interest in the land in question for compensation as held by the Ld. Court vide judgment Ex.PW4/A. ISSUE NO.2:
"What was the market value of land in question at the time of issuance of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act?
AND ISSUE NO.3 "Whether the petition is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
opennyai_summary.arguments: In support of this issue, petitioners have relied upon the reference judgment U/s 30-31, L.A. Act vide Ex.PW4/A wherein the share of the deceased petitioner- Sh. Nand Lal was determined to the extent of 20 sq.yds. to be divided in equal shares in favour of the petitioners- Raj Kumar and Om Prakash (both sons of Sh. Nand Lal).
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
During the course of argument,
counsels for the parties have apprised this Court that market value with respect to the land acquired vide the same notification and same award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 07.06.2019 passed in the case titled as "Union of India Vs. M.L. Gupta & Ors.' in which the Hon'ble High Court has fixed the market value of the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtr. along-with statutory benefits.
b) Since there is an authoritative pronouncement on the fair market value of the similar land placed in similar circumstances, LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs.
Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 11 of 14 location and topography and acquired vide the same award, this Court need not to delve further in this regard.
Even otherwise, two equals cannot be treated unequally.
In these circumstances, this Court is not inclined to go into any evidences or judgments relied upon by the parties to the instant petition in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court in case titled as 'Union of India Vs.
M.L. Gupta' wherein the market value for the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award have already been assessed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e. 12.06.1997.
Even otherwise, nothing substantial has been brought on record by either side to differ from the market value assessed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in one of the matters arising out of the same award and pertaining to the identical land.
Therefore, in the LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal &
Anr. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 12 of 14 totality of circumstances, it is held that market value of the land in question acquired vide the same notification and same award is fixed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtr. on the date of notification i.e. 12.06.1997 along-with statutory benefits.
ISSUE NO.4 "RELIEF"
a)
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners had claimed compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- per sq.mt., which is now fixed and allowed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mt.
The petitioners are entitled to the market value @ Rs.4692/- per ) Sh. Nand Lal (Since Deceased) vs Union Of India on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182853182/
8 sq.mt. as on 12.06.1997 with respect to their share determined in the total land acquired i.e. 16.72 sq. mtrs. (20 sq.yds.) as per the judgment in reference U/s 30-31, L.A. Act vide Ex.PW4/A.
b)
c) The petitioners have also claimed interest, as per law.
According to the award, 12% interest was allowed on the market value, fixed by the LAC U/s 23(1)A of LA Act, 1894 from the date of notification U/s 4 of Act (12.06.1997) till the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999.
Accordingly, the same is also allowed on the present market value, fixed as above.
d) According to the award, interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894 LAC No.44/16 Sh. Nand Lal & Anr. Vs.
Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 13 of 14 was also allowed observing that DMRC had taken the land on 12.06.1997 and as such petitioners are entitled to interest on the balance amount, as per section 34 of LA Act, 1894 @ 9% per annum from the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999 till expiry of one year and thereafter, @ 15% per annum till payment or deposited into the Court.
The same is also allowed on the enhanced market value of the land in question, as determined above.
The respondent nos.1 and 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation as determined hereinabove to the petitioners.
e) The above reliefs are subject to the deductions of compensation / solatium / additional benefits /
interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894, which have already been received by the petitioners/ LRs of petitioner, as were fixed by the LAC vide Award No. 01/1999-2000 dated 20.07.1999.
f)
The reference petition stands answered accordingly.
Both the parties will bear their own costs.
A copy of this judgment be sent to LAC concerned to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation to the petitioners within three months from today.
No order as to cost.
